data.narrative:
Asylon Robotics is a Series B drone and autonomous systems company that has raised $40M to date. The broader Drones & Autonomous sector includes eight private peers (Elroy Air, Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation among them) and no public comparables, limiting traditional peer benchmarking.

Stage-progression methodology was the only applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised ($40M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B-to-subsequent-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $76M. A peer-median approach was not viable; while five same-sector companies exist, fewer than three operate at comparable stage or valuation tier, making sector-wide medians uninformative for frontier-stage ventures.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $65M (low) to $87M (high), centered on $76M. This range reflects standard progression mechanics but carries material uncertainty. The single-method foundation reflects genuine data scarcity rather than false precision. Key risk factors include stage-multiplier sensitivity (the 1.9x assumption), absence of comparable-stage peer pricing, and nascent market maturity in autonomous systems. Investors should weight management execution, customer traction, and capital efficiency as offset to quantitative constraints in this valuation.
